burst_caption: Video bursts: mean 0.2 s ON / 0.8 s OFF
finding: QoS reduced control delay by 24% and video delay by 24%.
speaker_notes:
RTX 5090 experiment: brief video congestion, measured 14 Oct 2026 SGT. Source docs/reports/experiments/scheduler-bursty-load-20261014/README.md and summary.json. Four sequential runs RR, QoS, QoS, RR, each with 120 measurement seconds and six seconds of drain. One OCUDU gNB and two srsUEs. Both schedulers retain their original defaults.

Download UE: 5QI 9, 30 Mb/s constant DL plus 2 Mb/s UL. Interactive UE: 5QI 7, 40 Mb/s video during exponentially distributed ON periods averaging 0.2 s; OFF periods average 0.8 s. Control sends 200-byte packets every 10 ms in both directions. Mean ON/OFF durations are not fixed periodic slots. The expected downlink demand is 38.16 Mb/s including control; the peak is 70.16 Mb/s. Measured cell service capacity in the preceding stress test was about 57 Mb/s, so brief bursts compete for resources but average offered load can drain. Exact realized packet counts are recorded.

Relative to the preceding 70/40 Mb/s sustained overload, only download rate (70 to 30) and mean video ON/OFF duration (2/1 s to 0.2/0.8 s) change. No queue limit, drop policy or scheduler parameter was adjusted. Both policies use the same traffic seed, resources and channel scenario. All four runs are retained, not selected by effect size.

Bars show the arithmetic mean of each valid second’s p99 delivered-packet one-way UDP delay, averaged equally over two runs per policy. Empty video seconds are excluded. This is not pooled packet p99, maximum latency or scheduler execution time. All configured DL and UL packets arrive after drain. There are no full-RLC-queue log messages in any run.

RTX 5090, Core Ultra 9 285K, 20 MHz, 15 kHz SCS, 23.04 MS/s, CUDA channel, 23040-sample maximum batches, seed-1 moving robot-ring Sionna scenario at 10 Hz with configured 40 dB AWGN SNR. Affinity: gNB cores 0–7, both UEs share 8–19, broker 20, auxiliary work 22–23. Broker pacing remains enabled and redundant srsUE receive sleep disabled. IQ progress uses cumulative acquired samples over monotonic wall time.

QoS is the default OCUDU proportional-fair scheduler with priority, packet-delay-budget and GBR terms enabled, fairness exponent 2. The non-GBR formula on the slide is approximate; zero-wait and new-UE cases are omitted. Control/video share one default bearer on the interactive UE, so this is prioritization between UEs, not separate scheduling classes for video and control. Their 5QI 7 has 100 ms packet delay budget; download 5QI 9 has 300 ms. These are inputs, not guarantees. Source use_cases/scheduler_benchmark/definitions.py and the native OCUDU scheduler_time_qos.cpp.

Two repeats at one seed do not establish statistical significance or a general policy ranking. Small ray-solver numeric differences and uncontrolled host background activity remain. Starvation events remain recorded, so no strict zero-miss real-time qualification is claimed. The earlier overloaded case is retained in scheduler-priority-load-20261014.
